page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg8i.2xlarge is a member of the High Clock Speed instance family, built on the KVM hypervisor architecture using the x86_64 platform. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6462C processor operating at a nominal clock frequency of 3.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an exact ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core. No physical GPUs are equipped on this profile.

Network connectivity delivers an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and the profile provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Local disk storage is not bundled, indicating that operating system installations and workload persistence rely completely on external cloud storage volumes. Architectural deployments must account for storage network I/O demands against network capacity when hosting disk-intensive operations.

By offering dedicated cores clocked at 3.3 GHz alongside a balanced 1:4 memory allocation, the instance balances high per-thread compute capability with sufficient system memory. Cost efficiency centers on applications requiring strong sequential CPU performance without demanding specialized accelerators. Typical deployment scenarios include backend application hosting, compilation workflows, continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) runners, batch transaction processing, and relational database servers.

The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 6462C processor rated at 3.3 GHz, combined with 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included, and the instance provisions no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached cloud disks for persistent storage needs. Network connectivity is configured with an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth, though complimentary public IPv4 addressing is not bundled. Balancing elevated CPU clock frequencies with standard memory density, this instance targets compute tasks constrained by per-core execution speeds, including continuous integration pipelines, batch compute jobs, application compilation, mid-tier relational databases, and enterprise application backends requiring stable CPU execution.
